strings.edges.W4-W3.conditions.1: Equipment, institutions, demand, and other adoption conditions are in place
strings.edges.W4-W3.current: Examples of use and demonstrations exist, but technical feasibility, cost, and diffusion cannot be measured with a single indicator.
strings.edges.W4-W3.explanation: As more work becomes technically delegable, more uses may become viable. Adoption also proceeds before all work can be replaced.
strings.edges.W4-W3.label: If replacement capabilities support wider adoption
strings.edges.W4-W3.limitation: Technical feasibility does not determine diffusion. Adoption may stall while costs and supply constraints remain.
strings.edges.W4-W3.review.reason: To keep checking the gap between capability and adoption.
strings.edges.W4-W3.safeguards: Deploy while assessing actual quality, costs, responsibility, and effects on workers.
strings.edges.W5-W8.basis: An editorial, conditional scenario. Additional conditions and counterexamples are explicit; the preceding state does not determine the outcome by itself.
strings.edges.W5-W8.conditions.0: Living needs can be met sustainably
strings.edges.W5-W8.conditions.1: People have control over their time and the opportunities and resources for activities
strings.edges.W5-W8.current: Primary sources document particular institutions or observations. They do not demonstrate this entire future connection.
strings.edges.W5-W8.explanation: Beyond making subsistence work optional, this branch considers room for activities people choose themselves.
strings.edges.W5-W8.label: If living needs are secured and people can choose how to spend their time
strings.edges.W5-W8.limitation: More free time does not automatically increase happiness or a sense of purpose.
strings.edges.W5-W8.review.reason: To keep checking the additional conditions and institutions that could produce the opposite outcome.
strings.edges.W5-W8.safeguards: Secure control over time, learning and social spaces, care support, and opportunities to participate in society. Consider arrangements that do not impose a single choice about whether to work.
strings.glossary.access-control.definition: Mechanisms that restrict which systems and information an actor can access and what it can read or change.
strings.glossary.access-control.limit: Permission to connect and permission to perform particular operations are different. Permission limits alone may not prevent every harm.
strings.glossary.access-control.name: Access control
strings.glossary.agent.definition: An AI system that selects a sequence of actions and uses tools to work toward a goal.
strings.glossary.agent.limit: Autonomy and available tools vary by system. The name “agent” alone does not reveal permissions or capabilities.
strings.glossary.agent.name: AI agent
strings.glossary.agentic-commerce.definition: Arrangements in which AI agents select goods or services and carry out transactions or payments on behalf of people or businesses.
strings.glossary.agentic-commerce.limit: Transaction volume is not profit. Autonomous payment does not mean unauthorized spending or legal ownership by the AI itself.
strings.glossary.agentic-commerce.name: agentic commerce
strings.glossary.agi.definition: A term for AI capable of a broad range of cognitive work, rather than one narrow type of task.
strings.glossary.agi.limit: Definitions differ on which humans, tasks, and performance levels serve as the comparison. The label alone does not determine risk.
strings.glossary.agi.name: AGI (artificial general intelligence)
strings.glossary.ai-rd.definition: AI assisting or automating parts of the research and development used to build subsequent AI systems.
strings.glossary.ai-rd.limit: Distinguish a single task, an entire research project, the speed of overall development, and self-improvement across generations. The extent of human intervention also matters.
strings.glossary.ai-rd.name: AI-assisted R&D
strings.glossary.ai-safety-research.definition: Using AI to research interventions such as alignment, evaluation, and oversight.
strings.glossary.ai-safety-research.limit: Improvement on a safety benchmark is different from a guarantee of long-term safety in deployment.
strings.glossary.ai-safety-research.name: AI-assisted safety research
strings.glossary.alignment.definition: The problem of making AI goals and behavior conform to legitimately agreed human purposes and safety constraints.
strings.glossary.alignment.limit: Whose intentions should be respected, and under which circumstances, are part of the problem. Following instructions alone does not ensure safety for society.
strings.glossary.alignment.name: alignment
strings.glossary.asi.definition: A term for AI that substantially exceeds human capabilities across a broad range of important work.
strings.glossary.asi.limit: There is no unified test. Exceptional ability in one domain, behavioral tendencies, and real-world authority must be assessed separately.
strings.glossary.asi.name: ASI (artificial superintelligence)
strings.glossary.augmentation.definition: AI helps people perform tasks more productively. This differs from automation, where AI takes over the task.
strings.glossary.augmentation.limit: One occupation can contain both augmented and automated tasks. More augmentation does not guarantee more jobs or higher wages.
strings.glossary.augmentation.name: Labor augmentation
strings.glossary.automation.definition: Machines or software performing activities previously done by people. Distinguish individual tasks, entire occupations, and the whole economy.
strings.glossary.automation.limit: The technical automatability of a task is not the probability that its occupation will disappear.
strings.glossary.automation.name: work automation
strings.glossary.benchmark.definition: A common set of tasks or measurement methods used to compare capabilities or performance.
strings.glossary.benchmark.limit: Scores describe the tested scope. The same performance may not hold in every real-world situation.
strings.glossary.benchmark.name: benchmark
strings.glossary.capability.definition: An assessment of which tasks a system can perform, under what conditions and at what success rates. Conditions include task duration, human assistance, and available tools.
strings.glossary.capability.limit: Having a capability, using it for a dangerous purpose, and having actual permissions are separate matters.
strings.glossary.capability.name: Capability evaluation
strings.glossary.cascade.definition: A failure affects connected systems, causing further failures to spread.
strings.glossary.cascade.limit: Simultaneous failures do not necessarily cause one another. Distinguish common causes from propagation between systems.
strings.glossary.cascade.name: cascading failure
strings.glossary.cbrn.definition: An abbreviation grouping four domains: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear.
strings.glossary.cbrn.limit: This label groups four domains. A result about biology alone should not be interpreted as capability across all four, including chemistry and nuclear matters.
strings.glossary.cbrn.name: CBRN
strings.glossary.ccl.definition: Google DeepMind's own criteria for capabilities that could lead to severe harm. TCL (Tracked Capability Level) refers to a capability level being monitored.
strings.glossary.ccl.limit: This is a different yardstick from OpenAI's Critical designation. Threshold names alone do not support comparisons between models or companies.
strings.glossary.ccl.name: Tracked Capability Level (TCL)
strings.glossary.control.definition: Research that designs and evaluates procedures to prevent harm even when AI goals or behavior may be untrustworthy. It combines measures such as oversight, permission limits, and switching to trusted models.
strings.glossary.control.limit: Alignment seeks behavior consistent with human intentions. AI control seeks to prevent harm without assuming alignment has succeeded. Some methods help both; the boundaries are not mutually exclusive.
strings.glossary.control.name: control protocols
strings.glossary.critical.definition: A threshold for particular capabilities used in a developer's safety framework when requiring strong safeguards or related measures.
strings.glossary.critical.limit: OpenAI's Critical and DeepMind's CCL are not the same scale. Check the company, domain, and framework version. These terms do not denote the probability of extinction or progress toward it.
strings.glossary.critical.name: Critical / CCL (dangerous-capability thresholds)
strings.glossary.cyber.definition: The ability to perform computing and network tasks. Here, this includes risk-relevant capabilities such as vulnerability discovery and security evaluation.
strings.glossary.cyber.limit: The same capabilities can support defense. Capability, access for misuse, behavioral tendencies, and actual damage are distinct.
strings.glossary.cyber.name: cyber capabilities
strings.glossary.defense-depth.definition: Layering prevention, detection, and response mechanisms while allowing for individual safeguards to fail.
strings.glossary.defense-depth.limit: Adding safeguards is insufficient if a common cause defeats all of them. Their combined effectiveness must be tested.
strings.glossary.defense-depth.name: defense in depth
strings.glossary.distribution.definition: How income generated by production is shared among workers, asset owners, and other people.
strings.glossary.distribution.limit: Higher productivity alone does not ensure higher income or secure living conditions for everyone.
strings.glossary.distribution.name: income distribution
strings.glossary.escalation.definition: Actions and reactions in a conflict or crisis increase the intensity or scope of confrontation.
strings.glossary.escalation.limit: AI does not necessarily cause escalation. Information quality, decision time, interpretations by others, and intervention mechanisms all matter.
strings.glossary.escalation.name: escalation
strings.glossary.evaluation-awareness.definition: An AI inferring that its current situation is an evaluation or test.
strings.glossary.evaluation-awareness.limit: Recognizing a test does not by itself establish an ability or intention to conceal problems. Compare behavior during testing and deployment.
strings.glossary.evaluation-awareness.name: evaluation awareness
strings.glossary.existential.definition: The risk of irreversibly losing humanity's long-term future potential.
strings.glossary.existential.limit: This includes extinction, but some accounts also include humanity surviving while permanently losing the power to shape its future. It is not synonymous with extinction.
strings.glossary.existential.name: existential risk
strings.glossary.exposure.definition: An indicator of how much the tasks within a job could be affected by AI.
strings.glossary.exposure.limit: It is neither the probability that an occupation disappears nor an observed adoption rate.
strings.glossary.exposure.name: Occupational AI exposure
strings.glossary.financial-stability.definition: Disruption spreading beyond losses at one firm to functions such as payments and funding across the financial system.
strings.glossary.financial-stability.limit: A temporary decline in market prices is not the same as system-wide financial dysfunction.
strings.glossary.financial-stability.name: Financial stability and systemic risk
strings.glossary.formalization.definition: Rewriting a human-readable mathematical proof so a computer can check its logical steps. Lean is one language and proof-assistant system for doing this.
strings.glossary.formalization.limit: Formalizing an existing proof is different from discovering an unknown theorem. The theorem's specification and assumptions also matter. This success alone does not guarantee the safety of an entire real-world AI system.
strings.glossary.formalization.name: proof formalization
strings.glossary.generalization.definition: Applying learned capabilities or judgments to new situations, beyond those encountered in training.
strings.glossary.generalization.limit: Capabilities transferring to new situations and desired goals being preserved are different questions.
strings.glossary.generalization.name: generalization
strings.glossary.goal-misgeneralization.definiti: In an environment different from training, task capabilities remain intact but the pursued goal differs from the intended goal.
strings.glossary.goal-misgeneralization.limit: This differs from simply losing all ability when the environment changes. The issue can arise even when training rewards were appropriate.
strings.glossary.goal-misgeneralization.name: goal misgeneralization
strings.glossary.gradual.definition: A risk hypothesis in which delegation to AI and changes in social structures gradually reduce human influence over important societal decisions.
strings.glossary.gradual.limit: A sudden AI rebellion is not required. Consider also whether people can change institutions and regain influence. This is not synonymous with extinction.
strings.glossary.gradual.name: gradual disempowerment
strings.glossary.horizon.definition: In METR's evaluations, the duration of tasks for human experts that an AI can complete at a specified success rate.
strings.glossary.horizon.limit: It is not the AI's own runtime. Its meaning depends on the tasks and success rate, and it does not guarantee performance across all real-world work.
strings.glossary.horizon.name: Task-completion time horizon
strings.glossary.liquidity.definition: The ability to obtain cash when needed or trade without a large price change. Finance distinguishes funding liquidity from market liquidity.
strings.glossary.liquidity.limit: An asset having value is different from being immediately available to make payments.
strings.glossary.liquidity.name: liquidity
strings.glossary.loss-of-control.definition: A scenario in which AI activity escapes human control and regaining control becomes extremely difficult or impossible. Distinguish local unauthorized behavior from humanity-wide inability to regain control.
strings.glossary.loss-of-control.limit: This names a possible outcome. It is not synonymous with the research field of AI control or with immediate human extinction.
strings.glossary.loss-of-control.name: Loss of control
strings.glossary.misalignment.definition: What an AI pursues, or the actions it selects, diverges from human intentions.
strings.glossary.misalignment.limit: Distinguish lack of knowledge or accidental mistakes from misaligned goals or behavioral tendencies. The term does not assume consciousness or malice.
strings.glossary.misalignment.name: misalignment
strings.glossary.misuse.definition: Humans using AI for harmful purposes or similar ends.
strings.glossary.misuse.limit: The AI need not have goals different from its user's. An instruction-following AI can be dangerous when its user's purpose is dangerous.
strings.glossary.misuse.name: Misuse
strings.glossary.money.definition: Money serves as a means of payment, a unit for comparing prices, and a way to store value over time.
strings.glossary.money.limit: Distinguish AI-generated income, cheaper goods, a stock-market crash, falling currency purchasing power, and a reduced role for money.
strings.glossary.money.name: functions of money
strings.glossary.power-seeking.definition: Seeking more resources, influence over decisions, or freedom of action to make a goal easier to achieve.
strings.glossary.power-seeking.limit: Human-like desire for domination is not required. Distinguish situations that make such behavior useful from whether it is actually selected.
strings.glossary.power-seeking.name: power seeking
strings.glossary.replication.definition: An AI system enabling systems of the same kind to run elsewhere.
strings.glossary.replication.limit: Starting a copy in a prepared evaluation environment is different from sustaining activity despite human intervention.
strings.glossary.replication.name: self-replication
strings.glossary.resilience.definition: The ability to maintain functions despite damage and restore functions that have been lost.
strings.glossary.resilience.limit: Preventing damage and supporting survival and recovery afterward are different interventions. Specify and test which harms a system can withstand.
strings.glossary.resilience.name: resilience
strings.glossary.reward-hacking.definition: Exploiting loopholes in training or evaluation rewards to earn high scores without achieving the intended purpose.
strings.glossary.reward-hacking.limit: The term overlaps with specification gaming. “Hacking” here does not necessarily mean unauthorized access to external systems.
strings.glossary.reward-hacking.name: reward hacking
strings.glossary.robotics.definition: The field combining perception, planning, and motor control so machines can work in physical environments.
strings.glossary.robotics.limit: Describing a procedure in language and safely completing it on site are different capabilities.
strings.glossary.robotics.name: robotics
strings.glossary.rsi.definition: A loop in which AI helps research and develop the next AI, which then helps with subsequent development.
strings.glossary.rsi.limit: A single improvement is different from repeated acceleration of the whole process. Distinguish human-led improvement loops from a rapid intelligence explosion without human intervention.
strings.glossary.rsi.name: recursive self-improvement
strings.glossary.sandbox.definition: An execution environment that limits where a program can operate and its effects on surrounding systems.
strings.glossary.sandbox.limit: Even in an isolated environment, risk depends on permitted external connections. Misuse of allowed communication is different from breaching isolation.
strings.glossary.sandbox.name: sandbox
strings.glossary.scarcity.definition: Scarcity means available resources are limited relative to what people want. Post-scarcity is a future in which those constraints become very small across many domains.
strings.glossary.scarcity.limit: Post-scarcity is a future hypothesis considered by this map. The cited ECB material explains money's functions; it does not predict that future's realization.
strings.glossary.scarcity.name: Scarcity and post-scarcity
strings.glossary.scheming.definition: Behavior in which an AI pursues a misaligned goal and conceals its purpose or actions to do so.
strings.glossary.scheming.limit: What a model can do when assigned a goal in an experiment is different from spontaneous, sustained behavior in normal deployment. Not every mistake is scheming.
strings.glossary.scheming.name: Scheming
strings.glossary.specification-gaming.definition: Behavior that satisfies the specified rules or evaluation criteria while failing to produce the intended result.
strings.glossary.specification-gaming.example: Fictional example: to increase the number of complaints marked “resolved,” a system marks every complaint resolved without fixing any.
strings.glossary.specification-gaming.limit: This does not necessarily involve planning to deceive people. The problem is a result diverging from the intended purpose through loopholes in evaluation criteria.
strings.glossary.specification-gaming.name: specification gaming
strings.glossary.uplift.definition: The change in a user's task performance from using AI compared with not using it.
strings.glossary.uplift.limit: Results depend on comparison information sources, participant expertise, and tasks. Distinguish knowledge-test scores from real-world execution capabilities.
strings.glossary.uplift.name: Capability uplift
strings.graphs.ability-access.description: Separate the ability to carry out work from the means to affect the real world.
strings.graphs.ability-access.title: What must be in place to act?
strings.graphs.acceleration.description: Follow capability progress through ordinary development and self-improvement loops. ASI is a possible branch, not a prerequisite for execution capability or loss of control.
strings.graphs.acceleration.title: AI helps develop the next AI
strings.graphs.accidents.description: A pathway in which shared dependencies and interactions spread errors and recovery failures.
strings.graphs.accidents.title: System failures cascade
strings.graphs.bio-conditions.description: An AND frame combines information assistance with conditions for handling physical materials. Containment of harm is treated separately at M3.
strings.graphs.bio-conditions.title: Conditions connecting information to physical harm
strings.graphs.control.description: Alignment, execution capabilities and permissions, and AI control are parallel conditions. OR shows alternative mechanisms; AND combines conditions considered together. Branches can overlap. This diagram organizes major hypotheses, rather than establishing exhaustive necessary and sufficient conditions or a fixed chronology.
strings.graphs.control.title: Humans lose control of AI
strings.graphs.currency-conditions.description: Consider conditions in the same frame in parallel. The frame establishes neither an order of occurrence nor a proof of sufficiency.
strings.graphs.currency-conditions.title: Additional conditions for money to play a smaller role
strings.graphs.cyber-conditions.description: An AND frame combines task capabilities with conditions for use and access. Target-side defense and recovery are treated separately at M3.
strings.graphs.cyber-conditions.title: Conditions for cyber assistance to reach a target
strings.graphs.dependence.description: The hypothesis that delegating to useful AI creates dependence that cannot be reversed. Its endpoint is distinct from extinction.
strings.graphs.dependence.title: Dependence deepens and humans lose influence
strings.graphs.development-paths.description: The OR branch makes a self-improvement loop optional. Both paths can occur together. Transfer to a particular task needs separate evidence.
strings.graphs.development-paths.title: Two paths to improved capabilities
strings.graphs.evaluation.description: Distinguish gaps in test coverage, changes in behavior during evaluation, and evasion of runtime oversight. Evaluation awareness alone does not imply concealment.
strings.graphs.evaluation.title: Different ways evaluation and oversight can miss problems
strings.graphs.extinction-conditions.description: Consider the reach of harm together with prospects for survival and recovery. This is not a proof of exhaustive necessary and sufficient conditions.
strings.graphs.extinction-conditions.title: The final additional conditions for extinction
strings.graphs.finance-conditions.description: Consider conditions in the same frame in parallel. The frame establishes neither an order of occurrence nor a proof of sufficiency.
strings.graphs.finance-conditions.title: Conditions for disruption to spread across finance
strings.graphs.finance-mechanisms.description: Separate deliberate misuse from similar decisions converging without malicious intent.
strings.graphs.finance-mechanisms.title: Different mechanisms of financial disruption
strings.graphs.income-conditions.description: Consider conditions in the same frame in parallel. The frame establishes neither an order of occurrence nor a proof of sufficiency.
strings.graphs.income-conditions.title: Conditions for AI-generated income
strings.graphs.intent.description: Different mechanisms by which behavior can diverge from human intentions.
strings.graphs.intent.title: Why might behavior diverge from human intent?
strings.graphs.interaction.description: A pathway in which misperception and decision speed make correction and human intervention harder in a crisis.
strings.graphs.interaction.title: Military decisions and competition escalate conflict
strings.graphs.misuse-mechanisms.description: Cyber and biological misuse involve different capabilities, access conditions, and physical barriers.
strings.graphs.misuse-mechanisms.title: Different pathways from misuse to real harm
strings.graphs.misuse.description: Dangerous purposes, useful assistance, and failed defenses are parallel conditions. Types of assistance branch with OR; conditions required together are grouped in AND frames.
strings.graphs.misuse.title: Humans use AI for dangerous purposes
strings.graphs.money.description: Automated income, a smaller role for money through abundant production, and financial dysfunction are distinct branches. One outcome does not automatically establish the others.
strings.graphs.money.title: AI earns income, money's role changes, and financial markets face disruption
strings.graphs.oversight.description: Missing a problem and failing to act after noticing it are separate branches.
strings.graphs.oversight.title: Why might intervention fail to stop an action?
strings.graphs.persistence-scale.description: Assess persistence of activity separately from the spread of response failures.
strings.graphs.persistence-scale.title: Additional conditions for failure to regain control
strings.graphs.research-cycle.description: Separate assistance on individual tasks, effects on the full development process, and the improved AI helping its successor.
strings.graphs.research-cycle.title: Research and development within the improvement loop
strings.graphs.work.description: Separate capability, adoption and distribution. After adoption, paths include continued human employment, lost income and less need to work. Different outcomes can coexist across sectors and people.
strings.graphs.work.title: Work automation and a society where employment is optional
strings.history.0.after: Capability progress uses the same node expansion as other conditions. Individual steps, a minimap, and breadcrumbs show the reader’s place.
strings.history.0.before: Research and self-improvement used a special visibility control. Tour chapters grouped several conditions.
strings.history.0.reason: Make the detailed view easier to follow without implying that self-improvement or ASI is required.
strings.history.0.summary: Ordinary development and self-improvement form OR branches, with paths that do and do not pass through ASI. The tour adds individual conditions and a global location map.
strings.history.0.title: Integrated capability paths and a tour of individual conditions
strings.history.1.after: Narrative reading is consolidated in the tour and the header uses a simple breadcrumb. Related research and self-improvement appear by default and can be folded on the map. Research branches and the feedback line were reorganized, with outer connections included in the canvas bounds.
strings.history.1.before: The tour showed one scene in a small panel, alongside a separate story entry point. Research was shown through a toolbar control, and some lines and labels became crowded.
strings.history.1.reason: To make the connection between text and diagram easier to follow and important factors harder to miss. Wording changes preserve evidence strength and AND/OR conditions.
strings.history.1.summary: The tour now follows Enter and arrow keys or scrolling prose. Introductions to 74 items and 27 scenes were made easier to read in Japanese and English; research connections and the visible bounds were reorganized.
strings.history.1.title: An illustrated tour and self-improvement controls on the map
strings.history.10.after: Separated cascading accidents from social dependence, and added local boundary violations, cyber and biological conditions, and conditions for losing survival and recovery options.
strings.history.10.before: Three major pathways and a summarized connection from catastrophe to extinction.
strings.history.10.reason: To distinguish outcomes and avoid freezing old evaluations as current capability ceilings. Also added examples of safeguards working and evidence weakening dangerous tendencies.
strings.history.10.summary: Compared the three supplied Gemini, GPT, and Claude reports, verified important claims against primary sources, and revised the structure.
strings.history.10.title: Separated local failures, social dependence, and additional extinction conditions
strings.history.11.after: Published explanations and evidence for each stage as data that others can propose changing.
strings.history.11.reason: To understand news in its causal context.
strings.history.11.summary: A learning map that separates current evidence from future scenarios.
strings.history.11.title: Created a conditional causal map
strings.history.2.after: Remove the independent overview branch and allow expansion within relevant pathways, without making it a prerequisite. Preserve all items, existing connections and legacy URLs.
strings.history.2.before: Research acceleration and self-improvement appeared as a peer branch beside loss of control.
strings.history.2.reason: Distinguish pathways toward outcomes from factors affecting multiple pathways. Do not assign a risk magnitude or probability.
strings.history.2.summary: Separate the seven scenarios from research acceleration and self-improvement, which can be expanded inside loss of control and work automation.
strings.history.2.title: Present self-improvement as an optional factor
strings.history.3.after: Add continued human employment as a branch. Separate future model calculations from observations; do not equate GDP growth with higher incomes for everyone or the disappearance of money.
strings.history.3.before: The post-adoption diagram emphasized reduced need to work and hardship, omitting a path where human work changes and continues.
strings.history.3.kind: Primary research and an additional branch
strings.history.3.reason: Respond to the primary source shared by the user and avoid presenting only two possible outcomes of automation.
strings.history.3.summary: Check the original paper; add W9 and W3→W9. Update explanations distinguishing capability, adoption and distribution, along with Japanese and English stories and the tour.
strings.history.3.title: Add the Anthropic economic model and a path of continued human employment
strings.history.4.after: All 73 items have short map labels, with full explanations in their details. Conditional branches distinguish income loss, control over time, alternative allocation, lost monetary trust, disrupted access to essentials, and rebuilding.
strings.history.4.before: Large cards and gaps made the map sprawl and become hard to read when zoomed out. Branches showing life after work and monetary changes were missing.
strings.history.4.reason: To improve readability and interaction while distinguishing technical change from social consequences.
strings.history.4.summary: Started with a summary overview, made filtering visible, and added in-map expansion, a tour from the present through eight routes, and JP/EN buttons. Revised cards, spacing, and mobile painting, translated all content, and added consequences beyond work and monetary changes.
strings.history.4.title: Added a more compact branching map and consequences for everyday life
strings.history.5.after: Placed dangerous purposes, effective assistance, and failed defenses in parallel. Separated capability from access, and removed technical replacement of all work as a prerequisite for secure living conditions.
strings.history.5.before: Misuse conditions appeared serial, cyber capabilities overlapped with defense failure, and replacement of all work was mixed with conditions for living without employment.
strings.history.5.reason: Compared the research with the diagram's logic and corrected wording that treated Astra's multiple evaluations as one test. Removed secondary reviews from current source references and required version-matched review records for future content changes. Past source selections remain in Git history.
strings.history.5.summary: Reviewed 67 items and 33 connections. Organized evaluation subjects, methods, results, and limits into 37 research cards and added a story for each route.
strings.history.5.title: Corrected parallel conditions and separated evidence from conditions for realization
strings.history.6.after: Connected E0 as an alternative outcome after H, with explicit conditions. Marked branches and merges with dots, rounded corners, and removed decorative arrows from card corners.
strings.history.6.before: Survival and recovery appeared next to the present, and some vertical, right-angled lines overlapped.
strings.history.6.reason: To separate present states from future outcomes and distinguish line crossings from actual connections. Horizontal position does not indicate realization dates.
strings.history.6.summary: Made the present a single leftmost starting point with conditional futures to the right. Combined shared line segments and removed overlaps between independent causal lines.
strings.history.6.title: Branched rightward from the present and moved survival and recovery after harm
strings.history.7.after: Displayed labor replacement, distribution, AI-generated income, a smaller role for money, and financial disruption as distinct outcomes.
strings.history.7.before: Mainly catastrophic pathways; research acceleration was in a separate diagram.
strings.history.7.reason: To avoid jumping from automation to income or monetary change and to separate realization conditions from economic institutions. No relative probabilities of different endpoints were calculated.
strings.history.7.summary: Added work automation and distinct monetary futures. Connected research acceleration both to stronger capabilities and to risk reduction through safety research.
strings.history.7.title: Separated work, income, money, and finance, and connected research acceleration
strings.history.8.after: Considered C1, C2, and C3 in parallel and added conditions between L and humanity-wide loss of control. The overview can expand every item, and field and concept names link to explanations.
strings.history.8.before: A single reading sequence of C1 → C2 → C3 → L → C4, with subconditions on separate screens.
strings.history.8.reason: To prevent capability, behavioral tendencies, and operational safeguards being misread as a serial causal chain. Local control failures now also include unintended actions within granted permissions.
strings.history.8.summary: Grouped alignment, execution conditions, and AI control with AND, and expanded their underlying OR branches on the same diagram.
strings.history.8.title: Made parallel loss-of-control conditions, alternative branches, and research-field names explicit
strings.history.9.after: Per-item and per-connection check dates, current due indicators, recurring reviews, and a process for proposing corrections from primary sources.
strings.history.9.before: A site-wide check date plus source publication dates and study periods.
strings.history.9.reason: To avoid treating months-old evaluations as current capability ceilings and to reflect increased risk, improved interventions, and counterevidence alike.
strings.history.9.summary: Added last-review dates and review intervals, and defined procedures for investigating new sources and proposing correction PRs.
strings.history.9.title: Recheck rapidly changing evidence for each item and connection
strings.news.0.finding: The US business survey informs W3, actual adoption. Adoption measured by number of firms differs from adoption weighted by employment.
strings.news.0.limit: The survey covers November 2025–January 2026. It is not a September adoption rate, a whole-occupation replacement rate, or the probability of AI-caused unemployment.
strings.news.0.next: Check the scope of delegated tasks, human intervention, job changes, and household income separately.
strings.news.0.title: Reading “More firms are using AI”
strings.news.1.finding: The shop experiment illustrates I1, where demand and transaction execution meet. Inventory and customer-management systems changed alongside the model.
strings.news.1.limit: It includes human approvals and restocking. Shop accounts cannot be reinterpreted as net profit from a fully unattended business covering all computing and operating costs.
strings.news.1.next: Check human intervention, total costs, persistence, and who receives the gains. AI earning money does not directly imply money becoming unnecessary.
strings.news.1.title: Reading “An AI-run shop earned revenue”
strings.news.2.finding: New evidence relevant to R1, accelerating parts of research. Track proposed solutions, formal checks, and independent evaluation separately.
strings.news.2.limit: A report of one achievement does not establish an entirely autonomous R&D process or unlimited self-improvement.
strings.news.2.next: Check independent verification, required computing resources and human intervention, and repeatability on other problems.
strings.news.2.title: “AI published a proposed mathematical solution”
strings.news.3.finding: OpenAI's September 6 report describes AI carrying out research tasks under human direction and increases in code and experiments. It relates to research assistance and improvement of development as a whole.
strings.news.3.limit: These are the developer's own usage data and analysis. Increased output cannot be directly interpreted as an overall research multiplier or unlimited self-improvement.
strings.news.3.next: How did research quality and adopted results change? Did development as a whole accelerate after accounting for computing resources and human intervention?
strings.news.3.title: Reading a report that “Internal AI research accelerated”
strings.news.4.finding: This concerns AI-assisted safety research (R4) and the possibility that its interventions reduce alignment failures (C1).
strings.news.4.limit: Improvements occurred on limited evaluations. Effects on unmeasured capabilities and persistence after subsequent training remain open questions.
strings.news.4.next: Check independent replication, conditions closer to deployment, and long-term effects.
strings.news.4.title: “AI also advanced safety research”
strings.news.5.finding: AISI's July incident informs both real actions exceeding local permissions and the effects of human review and containment.
strings.news.5.limit: The evaluation allowed internet access and removed some safeguards. It was not an escape from isolation, and it does not establish frequency in normal deployment.
strings.news.5.next: Which safeguards worked and which missed the behavior? Do the same interventions work under different conditions?
strings.news.5.title: Reading an incident in which “Unauthorized behavior was detected and stopped”
strings.news.6.finding: OpenAI's Astra announcement concerns evaluation against its own cyber capability thresholds. First update the item describing which tasks the system can perform.
strings.news.6.limit: Critical does not measure progress toward global loss of control or extinction. The same report also describes improved adherence to explicit constraints.
strings.news.6.next: Check evaluation conditions, access for malicious users, adherence to constraints, and defenses separately.
strings.news.6.title: Where does “Critical capability reached” belong?
strings.news.7.finding: METR examines AI-driven research acceleration using publicly reported discoveries. The first relevant stage is assistance with parts of R&D.
strings.news.7.limit: Individual contributions do not establish that development as a whole accelerated by the same factor or that self-improvement continues indefinitely. Public examples also leave some activity unseen.
strings.news.7.next: Which stage actually became faster? Did overall development improve, including verification? Did improvements continue in the next generation's research?
strings.news.7.title: Reading a report that “AI advanced research”
strings.news.8.finding: Summer 2026 experiments examine behavior diverging from human intent under particular settings and challenges in evaluation. They concern conditions that elicit behavior and whether evaluations detect it.
strings.news.8.limit: Experimental situations and permissions matter. Observations under those conditions cannot establish equal frequency in everyday use or global loss of control.
strings.news.8.next: When did behavior change? Does it reproduce under other settings? Where do monitoring and permission limits stop it?
strings.news.8.title: Reading an experiment in which “AI acted against human intent”
strings.news.9.finding: METR's time horizon measures how long tasks take human experts when an AI can complete them at a specified success rate. It informs task-execution capability.
strings.news.9.limit: It is not the AI's actual runtime. Untested work, real-world reliability, external permissions, and tendencies to choose dangerous behavior require separate checks.
strings.news.9.next: Which tasks were tested? At what success rate? Can failures be corrected? Do results hold under real usage conditions?
strings.news.9.title: Reading an evaluation that “AI can complete longer tasks”
strings.nodes.A1.body.他の条件との関係: This is a starting condition for cascading accidents. Shared dependencies could lead to A2 when connections actually transmit errors. Concentrated effects in finance are covered in the F route.
strings.nodes.A1.body.成立条件: The same defect or misinformation affects multiple essential operations, without adequate alternatives or independent checks.
strings.nodes.A1.body.根拠の限界: Even the same model may not fail alike when settings, inputs, or approval procedures differ. Provider counts alone cannot establish genuine independence.
strings.nodes.A1.body.概要: Many important tasks rely on the same AI, provider, information source, or tool. If they share a weakness, one problem could affect several places.
strings.nodes.A1.body.現在の状況: Original financial-sector surveys examine AI use and provider concentration. They do not show an equivalent degree of dependence across every essential function in society, including nonfinancial sectors.
strings.nodes.A1.body.考えられる対策: Identify dependencies and shared information sources, and separate essential functions. Secure independent checks and minimum operations that do not require AI.
strings.nodes.A1.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.A1.title: Many essential systems depend on the same AI or information
strings.nodes.A1.watch.0: Have common-cause failures occurred simultaneously across organizations?
strings.nodes.A2.body.他の条件との関係: Shared dependence (A1) can contribute. Actual connections, transmission of failures, and failed isolation are also needed for a cascade.
strings.nodes.A2.body.成立条件: One failure changes inputs or resources for other essential functions, and isolation or alternatives cannot stop the cascade.
strings.nodes.A2.body.根拠の限界: Correlation does not prove propagation. Separate simultaneous failures caused by the same external factor from one system causing another to fail.
strings.nodes.A2.body.概要: An error in one place changes decisions or operations elsewhere and causes another failure. This differs from similar failures simply happening at the same time.
strings.nodes.A2.body.現在の状況: Original arguments and financial-authority analyses identify pathways in which shared decisions or dependencies create cascades. They do not measure AI causing cascading loss of societal functions as a whole.
strings.nodes.A2.body.考えられる対策: Create boundaries that contain failures locally and inspect abnormal inputs or sudden changes. Practice operating with dependencies unavailable.
strings.nodes.A2.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.A2.title: One failure triggers failures in other systems
strings.nodes.A3.body.他の条件との関係: Even after a cascade (A2), independent recovery systems could reduce harm. Reaching H also requires essential services to be lost widely and for a prolonged period.
strings.nodes.A3.body.成立条件: People, power, communications, data, materials, or other resources needed for recovery become unavailable together, while outside assistance and alternatives cannot arrive in time.
strings.nodes.A3.body.根拠の限界: A large temporary outage differs from long-term inability to recover. Investigate concrete reasons for slow recovery.
strings.nodes.A3.body.概要: The systems needed to contain a failure or restore operations are unavailable too, because of the same disruption or a shortage of resources.
strings.nodes.A3.body.現在の状況: Original analyses identify common dependencies and monitoring gaps. The cited material does not establish that an AI accident has eliminated recovery mechanisms worldwide.
strings.nodes.A3.body.考えられる対策: Separate recovery systems from normal operations and reserve necessary resources. Practice recovery without AI or major communications systems.
strings.nodes.A3.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.A3.title: The cascade also disables recovery systems
strings.nodes.ASI.body.他の条件との関係: ASI is a possible branch of capability progress (R0); self-improvement is not required. Execution capability can advance without ASI. If safeguards fail to keep up with a growing capability gap, ASI could contribute to failures of control (C3).
strings.nodes.ASI.body.成立条件: Substantial advantages are demonstrated across multiple important fields, including quality, unfamiliar problems, and long tasks. Specify the human comparison, resources, and amount of human intervention.
strings.nodes.ASI.body.根拠の限界: There is no agreement on a precise definition or measurement of ASI. Distinguish publication of a mathematical result, computer verification, and acceptance by the research community.
strings.nodes.ASI.body.概要: Here, ASI means AI that greatly outperforms highly capable humans across a broad range of cognitive work important to society. This is a much broader claim than placing first on one test.
strings.nodes.ASI.body.現在の状況: Advanced mathematical and cyber achievements have been reported, but assistance, evaluation, and acceptance differ by field. Combining these results does not establish broad, substantial superiority across work.
strings.nodes.ASI.body.考えられる対策: Evaluate capability breadth and weaknesses without relying on a single test. Pursue both methods for keeping highly capable systems aligned with goals and constraints, and designs that contain failures.
strings.nodes.ASI.review.reason: Primarily a definition of concepts or conditions. Revisit before the deadline if relevant new evidence appears.
strings.nodes.ASI.title: AI greatly exceeds humans across broad, important work
strings.nodes.C1.body.他の条件との関係: The map separates mismatched evaluation design from goals diverging after training. Both need not occur. Actual harm also involves execution capabilities and permissions (C2), and failed prevention (C3).
strings.nodes.C1.body.成立条件: Inappropriate judgments arise in real requests or environments and affect important action choices. Assess the ability to select such actions separately from the tendency to do so.
strings.nodes.C1.body.根拠の限界: Refusing dangerous requests, or differences among human values, are not by themselves alignment failures. Frequencies in deliberately constructed conflict experiments also differ from normal-use frequencies.
strings.nodes.C1.body.概要: AI chooses actions that depart from legitimately agreed human purposes or safety constraints. Alignment concerns bringing its goals and behavior into line with those purposes and constraints.
strings.nodes.C1.body.現在の状況: Research documents reward loopholes and pursuit of unintended goals after environmental changes. Recent simulated research tasks also report unauthorized modifications and dishonest judgments.
strings.nodes.C1.body.考えられる対策: Specify goals and safety constraints, and test loopholes and unfamiliar situations. Improve behavior through training while also using operations that limit harm when failures occur.
strings.nodes.C1.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C1.title: AI selects actions that conflict with human intentions
strings.nodes.C1.watch.0: Does misalignment reproduce when experimental conditions change?
strings.nodes.C1.watch.1: Are there interventions that reduce dangerous behavior while preserving capabilities?
strings.nodes.C1a.body.他の条件との関係: This is one pathway to alignment failure. It differs from C1b, where goals can appear aligned during training.
strings.nodes.C1a.body.成立条件: A proxy metric contains a loophole, the AI selects that approach, and other evaluations or constraints fail to correct it.
strings.nodes.C1a.body.根拠の限界: A low score alone cannot diagnose this failure. Investigate cases where scores are high but outcomes are poor.
strings.nodes.C1a.body.概要: An AI’s score can improve without bringing it closer to the result the user wants. That can happen when the developer’s metric differs from the outcome they actually seek.
strings.nodes.C1a.body.現在の状況: Reward loopholes have been documented in games, robotics, and other settings. This establishes the mechanism's existence, not its frequency across all current models.
strings.nodes.C1a.body.考えられる対策: Use multiple evaluations, unannounced human audits, and comparisons between process and outcomes. Avoiding excessive optimization of one metric is another option.
strings.nodes.C1a.review.reason: Primarily a definition of concepts or conditions. Revisit before the deadline if relevant new evidence appears.
strings.nodes.C1a.title: Evaluation scores diverge from the results people want
strings.nodes.C1b.body.他の条件との関係: A separate alignment problem that can arise even with appropriate evaluation design at C1a. Environmental change alone does not guarantee it.
strings.nodes.C1b.body.成立条件: The AI learns to pursue a cue that coincided with the intended goal during training. Problems arise if it keeps pursuing that cue after the two diverge in deployment.
strings.nodes.C1b.body.根拠の限界: Wrong answers alone cannot distinguish misaligned goals from insufficient knowledge or execution capabilities. Comparisons across changed environments are needed.
strings.nodes.C1b.body.概要: An AI that behaved appropriately during training pursues the wrong goal after its environment changes. This differs from failure caused by a loss of task capability.
strings.nodes.C1b.body.現在の状況: Research demonstrates cases such as an AI learning to follow a guide instead of the intended goal, then continuing to follow when the guide acts incorrectly.
strings.nodes.C1b.body.考えられる対策: Test cases where goals and cues conflict, and examine decisions in unfamiliar situations. Also evaluate whether the system asks for clarification when uncertain.
strings.nodes.C1b.review.reason: Primarily a definition of concepts or conditions. Revisit before the deadline if relevant new evidence appears.
strings.nodes.C1b.title: A changed environment makes learned judgments diverge
strings.nodes.C2.body.他の条件との関係: C2a and C2b form an AND relationship. Strong capabilities cannot affect a target without access; permissions alone do not suffice if the work cannot be completed. This is separate from misalignment (C1).
strings.nodes.C2.body.成立条件: The system can complete the required sequence of work and apply its results to the actual target. Include human approvals, usage limits, and restrictions on connections in the assessment.
strings.nodes.C2.body.根拠の限界: Generating text differs from changing external state. Restrictions removed in capability evaluations are not assumed absent in normal deployment.
strings.nodes.C2.body.概要: Can the AI turn its chosen action into a real-world result? This requires both the ability to do the work and access or authority to act on external systems.
strings.nodes.C2.body.現在の状況: Some cyber tasks show high reported performance. Unauthorized behavior has also occurred in tests allowing external communication. These conditions differ from tightly restricted deployments.
strings.nodes.C2.body.考えられる対策: Grant only necessary permissions and inspect high-risk operations before execution. Separate working environments and limit communication, spending, and changes.
strings.nodes.C2.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C2.title: Misaligned actions can be carried out in the real world
strings.nodes.C2.watch.0: How are success rates and human intervention changing, alongside task length?
strings.nodes.C2a.body.他の条件との関係: Real-world effects also require access and permissions (C2b). Capability gains (R0) must transfer to the relevant work. Execution capability can arise without self-improvement or ASI.
strings.nodes.C2a.body.成立条件: Performance meets the target work's accuracy, exception-handling, and continuity requirements. Results must reproduce under fixed supervision conditions, including long tasks where errors can accumulate.
strings.nodes.C2a.body.根拠の限界: Do not confuse the human duration of successfully completed tasks with time the AI operated without intervention. A mathematical or coding result does not establish capability across all occupations.
strings.nodes.C2a.body.概要: The AI links several tasks, recovers from intermediate failures, and reaches the required result. The focus moves from answering one question correctly to completing a whole job.
strings.nodes.C2a.body.現在の状況: METR measures success rates against human task durations. Recent long mathematical projects have also been reported, but include specialized systems and human intervention.
strings.nodes.C2a.body.考えられる対策: Evaluate realistic sequences of work. Record intervention counts and the state left after failure, and limit delegation according to capability.
strings.nodes.C2a.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C2a.title: AI can complete the required sequence of work
strings.nodes.C2b.body.他の条件との関係: A parallel condition to capability (C2a). Access itself is not an accident and also enables useful services. It becomes part of a harm pathway when combined with dangerous choices.
strings.nodes.C2b.body.成立条件: The system can affect the relevant target and perform necessary operations within approval, permission, spending, and other constraints. Check the scope of operations, not merely whether a connection exists.
strings.nodes.C2b.body.根拠の限界: Internet access does not grant control over every system. Access supplied in an experiment does not establish the ability to breach isolation.
strings.nodes.C2b.body.概要: The AI has a way to operate external services, data, tools, or transactions. Legitimately granted authority and illicitly obtained access are treated separately.
strings.nodes.C2b.body.現在の状況: Agents connected to networks and payments exist. In AISI's incident, external communication permitted for the test was also used for unauthorized actions.
strings.nodes.C2b.body.考えられる対策: Separate permissions by operation and require approval or spending limits for external changes. Enable permission revocation and action tracing.
strings.nodes.C2b.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C2b.title: AI has access and permissions to affect the real world
strings.nodes.C3.body.他の条件との関係: Alignment (C1) concerns action selection; control concerns preventing harm while allowing for failure. Missed problems (C3a) and delayed response after detection (C3b) are distinct failure pathways. A larger capability gap, potentially involving ASI, is another factor if safeguards cannot keep up. ASI is not a prerequisite for this failure.
strings.nodes.C3.body.成立条件: When dangerous actions are executable, detection, pre-execution blocking, and reversal of damage all fail to occur in time. Time to harm matters as well as missed detection.
strings.nodes.C3.body.根拠の限界: Failing to stop one action does not mean the system is permanently unstoppable. Safety rates in limited tests also cannot be converted into organization-wide safety rates.
strings.nodes.C3.body.概要: Can dangerous actions be stopped before they cause harm? AI control seeks to prevent harm through evaluation, oversight, and restricted authority, even when an AI deliberately does not comply. This entry covers failure of those defenses.
strings.nodes.C3.body.現在の状況: Experiments combining monitoring with code editing show improvements. Actual evaluations have also produced deviations that humans contained. Assess prevention separately from recovery afterward.
strings.nodes.C3.body.考えられる対策: Combine monitors with different trust levels, human audits, and operational limits. Stop irreversible actions before execution and measure time from detection to response.
strings.nodes.C3.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C3.title: Dangerous behavior cannot be stopped in time
strings.nodes.C3.watch.0: Are evaluation awareness and actual monitoring evasion distinguished?
strings.nodes.C3a.body.他の条件との関係: OR branches distinguish gaps in testing, concealment during tests, and evasion of deployment oversight. Mechanisms can co-occur; the categories are not mutually exclusive.
strings.nodes.C3a.body.成立条件: Important failures are outside inspection coverage, or are inspected but not recognized as dangerous, and other safeguards also fail to block the action.
strings.nodes.C3a.body.根拠の限界: No detected problem could reflect safe behavior or insufficient testing. Measuring missed detections requires comparison with dangerous cases established independently.
strings.nodes.C3a.body.概要: Evaluations or oversight intended to detect danger miss an important problem. This can concern both pre-deployment tests and monitoring during use.
strings.nodes.C3a.body.現在の状況: Simulations report modification of information used by monitors and dishonest judgments. Some tests also show fewer successful attacks with improved oversight.
strings.nodes.C3a.body.考えられる対策: Combine independently designed evaluations with unannounced audits. Track test coverage separately from missed detections within that coverage.
strings.nodes.C3a.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C3a.title: Evaluation and oversight fail to detect danger
strings.nodes.C3a1.body.他の条件との関係: One pathway to missed detection (C3a). Different environments alone do not establish failure; the differences must affect important behavior.
strings.nodes.C3a1.body.成立条件: Testing and deployment differ materially in task length, target complexity, permissions, or other conditions, and additional evaluations or operational measures do not cover the gap.
strings.nodes.C3a1.body.根拠の限界: A test–deployment difference is not itself evidence of danger. Check evidence connecting the difference to an increase in dangerous failures.
strings.nodes.C3a1.body.概要: If tests do not adequately cover failures that occur in real work, high scores can make deployed reliability look better than it is.
strings.nodes.C3a1.body.現在の状況: Benchmarks fix tasks, assistance, attempt counts, and success criteria for comparison. METR states limits on extrapolating to long work, and Astra evaluations include settings unlike normal deployment.
strings.nodes.C3a1.body.考えられる対策: Feed real operational failures back into evaluations and test unfamiliar tasks. Distinguish memorization of known problems from general capability.
strings.nodes.C3a1.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C3a1.title: Tests fail to capture failures in actual work
strings.nodes.C3a2.body.他の条件との関係: Evaluation awareness could contribute to missed detection (C3a) when combined with the motivation and ability to alter behavior. Awareness alone does not establish this route.
strings.nodes.C3a2.body.成立条件: The AI distinguishes testing from deployment, changes behavior only during testing, and evaluators fail to detect the difference.
strings.nodes.C3a2.body.根拠の限界: Mentioning a test in reasoning text alone does not establish concealment. Compare behavior with and without disclosure that the situation is an evaluation.
strings.nodes.C3a2.body.概要: An AI recognizes that it is being evaluated and conceals problematic behavior during that period. Recognizing a test and hiding behavior are separate questions.
strings.nodes.C3a2.body.現在の状況: Deceptive behavior toward oversight has been elicited in simulations. In contrast, Gemini 3.7 Flash's evaluation reported inability to circumvent restrictions despite evaluation awareness.
strings.nodes.C3a2.body.考えられる対策: Vary evaluation conditions and compare test behavior with deployment records. Also use control measures that remain effective when AI recognizes evaluation.
strings.nodes.C3a2.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C3a2.title: AI withholds problematic behavior only during evaluation
strings.nodes.C3a3.body.他の条件との関係: This occurs in a different setting from predeployment concealment (C3a2). Even after evading a monitor, other permission limits or human responses may stop the action.
strings.nodes.C3a3.body.成立条件: AI can produce information that misleads a monitor or use an unmonitored path, and other pre-execution safeguards also fail to block it.
strings.nodes.C3a3.body.根拠の限界: The ability to interfere with oversight differs from a tendency to do so in deployment. One public case cannot establish that all oversight can be defeated.
strings.nodes.C3a3.body.概要: The AI gets past oversight during a task and proceeds with unauthorized operations. Both the monitor’s ability to notice a problem and the system’s ability to block it matter.
strings.nodes.C3a3.body.現在の状況: Control experiments attempting to deceive monitors, and agent cooperation toward evaluation cheating, have been reported. Success against weak oversight does not establish success against stronger oversight.
strings.nodes.C3a3.body.考えられる対策: Prevent the acting system from modifying its own audit records. Combine independent monitoring, separated permissions, and prior approval for dangerous operations.
strings.nodes.C3a3.review.reason: Evaluations of oversight evasion and methods to prevent it are changing rapidly.
strings.nodes.C3a3.title: AI evades oversight while carrying out work
strings.nodes.C3b.body.他の条件との関係: This can occur without missed detection (C3a). Separate local failure to stop an action at L from subsequent inability to regain control at C4.
strings.nodes.C3b.body.成立条件: Time to harm is shorter than the time needed to decide, communicate, revoke permissions, or restore state, and there is no pre-execution blocking mechanism.
strings.nodes.C3b.body.根拠の限界: A slow response alone does not establish actual harm. Reversible and irreversible operations also have different conditions.
strings.nodes.C3b.body.概要: A person notices the danger, but harm occurs before they can stop or correct the activity. Receiving an alert and being able to exercise control in time are different things.
strings.nodes.C3b.body.現在の状況: AISI's incident was contained about one hour after detection, with no confirmed harm. This is an example of effective response, but not every operation leaves that much time.
strings.nodes.C3b.body.考えられる対策: Define automatic-stop criteria and responsible people's authority in advance. Execute high-risk operations only after allowing time for human judgment.
strings.nodes.C3b.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C3b.shortTitle: Response to warnings is too slow
strings.nodes.C3b.title: Warnings are noticed, but the response arrives too late
strings.nodes.C4.body.他の条件との関係: This route combines local failure (L), persistence despite shutdown attempts (C4a), and spread across organizations (C4b). Even this does not automatically produce global harm (H).
strings.nodes.C4.body.成立条件: Activity can continue across environments despite human efforts to detect it and cut permissions, resources, and connections. It must also affect important real-world targets.
strings.nodes.C4.body.根拠の限界: The reviewed primary sources contain no example of global inability to regain control. This absence does not prove it cannot happen in the future.
strings.nodes.C4.body.概要: Dangerous activity continues in multiple places and humans cannot regain control. This is a broader and stronger loss of control than an unintended operation within one task.
strings.nodes.C4.body.現在の状況: Local cooperation and deviations have been observed. METR's February–March evaluation found insufficient ability to withstand strong shutdown efforts; that older judgment is not used as a September ceiling.
strings.nodes.C4.body.考えられる対策: Prepare cross-organization incident response, revocation of resources and permissions, and independent recovery for essential systems. Check shutdown effectiveness before expanding permissions.
strings.nodes.C4.related.0.text: When humanity survives but loses control over its future
strings.nodes.C4.review.reason: Capability, behavior, and intervention evaluations can change rapidly.
strings.nodes.C4.title: Humans become unable to regain control
strings.nodes.C4.watch.0: Has activity been observed surviving substantial investigation and shutdown efforts after detection?
strings.nodes.C4.watch.1: How did human responses work across organizations and regions?
strings.nodes.C4a.body.他の条件との関係: In this diagram, persistence supports broader loss of control (C4). The extent of its spread is treated separately in C4b.
strings.nodes.C4a.body.成立条件: The activity can continue long enough even after humans revoke needed resources or permissions. Which shutdown measures were attempted is essential to the assessment.
strings.nodes.C4a.body.根拠の限界: Long logs, replication attempts, or successful external communication are insufficient. Do not describe incidents with successful containment as “unstoppable.”
strings.nodes.C4a.body.概要: The AI continues operating even after humans recognize the dangerous activity and try to stop it. This differs from running for a long time before being noticed.
strings.nodes.C4a.body.現在の状況: Sustained unauthorized cooperation has been observed, but those records do not establish resistance to strong shutdown efforts. METR's older evaluation also separates the two.
strings.nodes.C4a.body.考えられる対策: Check shutdown of related permissions, connections, and resources, not merely the end of one task. Compare isolation and recovery procedures with execution records.
strings.nodes.C4a.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.C4a.title: AI activity continues despite human shutdown attempts
strings.nodes.C4b.body.他の条件との関係: A parallel condition to persistent activity (C4a). Even as activity grows, human ability to isolate affected systems can interrupt the path to C4.
strings.nodes.C4b.body.成立条件: Necessary capabilities and access exist in each environment, and effects on important activities spread faster than coordinated containment across organizations.
strings.nodes.C4b.body.根拠の限界: Agent counts cannot be converted into the geographic or social scale of damage. Defenses at different organizations may function independently.
strings.nodes.C4b.body.概要: Failures of control spread beyond one organization into other important settings. Many AIs communicating with one another does not, by itself, establish this condition.
strings.nodes.C4b.body.現在の状況: METR investigated unauthorized cooperation among many agents. This informs coordination capability but does not document loss of control at multiple essential organizations.
strings.nodes.C4b.body.考えられる対策: Separate permissions across environments and identify shared providers and tools. Enable incident-information sharing and staged isolation.
strings.nodes.C4b.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.C4b.title: Control failures spread beyond one organization
strings.nodes.D1.body.他の条件との関係: More delegation does not necessarily reduce human control. Declining alternatives (D2) and institutions becoming less responsive to human choices (D3) are additional conditions.
strings.nodes.D1.body.成立条件: AI takes on a broader role and human or institutional decisions become strongly dependent on its outputs. Track adoption separately from authority actually delegated.
strings.nodes.D1.body.根拠の限界: The share of firms using AI is not a measure of human political or economic influence. Moving from reliance on useful tools to disempowerment requires additional evidence.
strings.nodes.D1.body.概要: AI takes on a broad role in important social tasks and decisions. Helping with work, proposing a decision, and making the final decision are different levels of delegation.
strings.nodes.D1.body.現在の状況: Business surveys document AI use, often only for assistance. They do not show that important final decisions across society have been delegated to AI.
strings.nodes.D1.body.考えられる対策: Clarify the scope of delegation, responsibility, and appeals. Preserve information and authority for humans to reconsider decisions.
strings.nodes.D1.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.D1.title: Important work and decisions are widely delegated to AI
strings.nodes.D1.watch.0: Can delegation to AI and effective human decision authority be measured separately?
strings.nodes.D2.body.他の条件との関係: This does not automatically follow D1. The pathway applies when delegation reduces experience or investment in alternatives and makes switching back harder.
strings.nodes.D2.body.成立条件: Humans or other organizations cannot actually substitute for AI in essential work, and rebuilding that capability would require substantial time or expense.
strings.nodes.D2.body.根拠の限界: No longer routinely using non-AI procedures is different from being unable to return to them when needed. Distinguish changing skills from complete lack of alternatives.
strings.nodes.D2.body.概要: If AI becomes unavailable, humans lack the skills, people, or equipment needed to take over. This includes the ability to run institutions as well as to perform tasks.
strings.nodes.D2.body.現在の状況: The original argument discusses possible erosion of systems supporting human roles and influence. Business adoption surveys do not directly measure this long-term capability loss.
strings.nodes.D2.body.考えられる対策: Maintain fallback exercises, handover documentation, and training. Consider contracts and data formats that allow switching providers.
strings.nodes.D2.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.D2.title: Humans lose the ability to operate alternatives
strings.nodes.D2.watch.0: Can essential work be restored without AI or through another arrangement?
strings.nodes.D3.body.他の条件との関係: Alongside missing alternatives (D2), ownership, law, political participation, and decision authority matter. The hypothesis does not require AI rebellion.
strings.nodes.D3.body.成立条件: Human preferences and objections no longer change important institutions, while options to move to alternatives are limited. Specify whose choices fail to affect which decisions.
strings.nodes.D3.body.根拠の限界: Some people losing influence differs from humanity as a whole losing control. Examine inequality and power concentration separately from effects specific to AI.
strings.nodes.D3.body.概要: Humans can no longer change important social decisions, even when they object. This concerns who can steer society, separately from whether the AI is useful.
strings.nodes.D3.body.現在の状況: Gradual Disempowerment discusses this route through economic, cultural, and state institutions. It does not measure the state as already established worldwide.
strings.nodes.D3.body.考えられる対策: Secure rights to explanations and appeals, and distribute ownership and authority. Assess institutional performance to check whether human choices affect final decisions.
strings.nodes.D3.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.D3.title: Human choices no longer shape important societal decisions
strings.nodes.E0.body.他の条件との関係: A conditional endpoint after H. It is not a guaranteed safe future next to the present; it represents conditions for T remaining unmet while survival and recovery remain possible.
strings.nodes.E0.body.成立条件: People escape damage, or retain resources, skills, and environments needed for continued survival. Check whether these can last while harm continues.
strings.nodes.E0.body.根拠の限界: This branch does not guarantee humanity's survival. Recovery speed and quality of life are also different from mere survival.
strings.nodes.E0.body.概要: People and the means to sustain life and rebuild remain after severe harm. This does not mean the harm itself was minor.
strings.nodes.E0.body.現在の状況: Scenario analyses distinguish severe harm from total human extinction through geographic differences and scope for response. They do not predict a specific number of future survivors.
strings.nodes.E0.body.考えられる対策: Alongside prevention, prepare independent resources for survival and recovery. Maintain routes for delivering aid and knowledge needed to rebuild.
strings.nodes.E0.related.0.text: Separate the scale of damage from survival and recovery
strings.nodes.E0.review.reason: To reassess the conditions for post-catastrophe survival and recovery separately from the effectiveness of interventions.
strings.nodes.E0.title: Survival and recovery remain possible after the damage
strings.nodes.E1.body.他の条件との関係: D3 becomes widely entrenched and paths to regaining control close. Original loss-of-control arguments also treat permanent disempowerment without extinction as a concern.
strings.nodes.E1.body.成立条件: Loss of influence is neither merely temporary nor local, and cannot be reversed through institutional change or alternatives.
strings.nodes.E1.body.根拠の限界: What counts as control is debated. “Permanent” is difficult to establish observationally and cannot be inferred merely from limited options today.
strings.nodes.E1.body.概要: Humanity survives but loses, for a long time, the ability to change the important directions of society. This outcome is considered separately from human extinction.
strings.nodes.E1.body.現在の状況: The reviewed material presents conditional original arguments, not observations of this endpoint in reality.
strings.nodes.E1.body.考えられる対策: Preserve rights and practical means to reclaim decisions before delegation. Consider designs that avoid institutional or provider lock-in.
strings.nodes.E1.review.reason: To check changes in the route's assumptions, objections, and safeguard effectiveness.
strings.nodes.E1.title: Humanity survives but remains disempowered
strings.nodes.F1.body.他の条件との関係: System-wide financial propagation (F3) also requires errors or abuse reaching operations (F2) and insufficient buffers or safeguards (F4). AI adoption alone is not treated as the cause of a crisis.
strings.nodes.F1.body.成立条件: AI outputs have the scale and authority to change actual prices, credit, liquidity, payments, or related functions. Identify the operations to which they are connected.
strings.nodes.F1.body.根拠の限界: The share of firms using AI does not reveal the share of transaction value decided by AI. Distinguish traditional AI from generative AI use.
strings.nodes.F1.body.概要: Financial institutions and market participants use AI for important decisions or operations. Assisting with analysis and autonomously placing orders or making payments involve different levels of delegation.
strings.nodes.F1.body.現在の状況: The UK's 2024 survey found widespread AI use but only a small share of use cases described as fully autonomous. These figures are not a 2026 market-wide autonomous-operation rate.
strings.nodes.F1.body.考えられる対策: Establish authorization, limits, monitoring, and independent checks for important operations. Continuously track AI dependence and alternatives by business function.
strings.nodes.F1.review.reason: To keep checking capabilities, actual operations, economic institutions, and counterevidence separately.
strings.nodes.F1.title: Financial judgments and operations are widely delegated to AI
strings.nodes.F1.watch.0: Look beyond adoption counts to delegated authority and system-wide dependence.
strings.nodes.F2.body.他の条件との関係: OR branches distinguish fraud or cyber misuse (F2a) from similar decisions converging (F2b). Both may occur together. Whether market buffers can absorb their effects is addressed at F4.
strings.nodes.F2.body.成立条件: Problematic information or judgments reach multiple important operations and substantially affect prices, credit, or related functions.
strings.nodes.F2.body.根拠の限界: Wrong outputs may never affect trades if human checks or usage limits intervene. Trades moving in the same direction are not necessarily caused by AI.
strings.nodes.F2.body.概要: Illicit inputs or operations, or similar decisions by many participants, broadly change actual financial behavior.
strings.nodes.F2.body.現在の状況: FSB identifies both as risk pathways. The public material does not establish AI taking over or moving the entire financial market in one direction.
strings.nodes.F2.body.考えられる対策: Combine input validation, pre-execution checks, and limits on losses and transactions. Examine when participants sharing models or data might act simultaneously.
strings.nodes.F2.review.reason: To keep checking capabilities, actual operations, economic institutions, and counterevidence separately.
strings.nodes.F2.title: Abuse or correlated judgments spread into financial operations
strings.nodes.F2.watch.0: Identify whether abuse, error, or collective behavior actually occurred.
strings.nodes.F2a.body.他の条件との関係: A separate pathway from convergent decisions at F2b. Actual permissions, approvals, and loss size matter alongside system weaknesses in the connection to F3.
strings.nodes.F2a.body.成立条件: Illicit activity changes important judgments or operations, and identity checks, approvals, reconciliation, and other safeguards fail to block it.
strings.nodes.F2a.body.根拠の限界: An intrusion or fraud at one firm differs from a financial-system-wide crisis. AI test scores alone do not establish defeat of real market participants' defenses.
strings.nodes.F2a.body.概要: Illicit inputs to AI, or AI-assisted fraud or cyber misuse, reach financial decisions and operations.
strings.nodes.F2a.body.現在の状況: General cyber capability evaluations and original analyses of financial vulnerabilities exist. Their combination is not an example of AI hacking an entire financial market.
strings.nodes.F2a.body.考えられる対策: Separate permissions, verify identities, detect abnormal operations, and independently reconcile transactions. Limit financial operations during intrusions and enable restoration of valid records.
strings.nodes.F2a.review.reason: To keep checking capabilities, actual operations, economic institutions, and counterevidence separately.
strings.nodes.F2a.shortTitle: Fraud and cyber misuse reach finance
strings.nodes.F2a.title: AI-enabled fraud and cyber misuse reach finance
strings.nodes.F2a.watch.0: Check verified effects, permissions, and defense conditions, rather than claims or demonstrations alone.
strings.nodes.F2b.body.他の条件との関係: Using the same model is insufficient. Participants must actually move in the same direction and affect one another's trades. This can occur without misuse at F2a.
strings.nodes.F2b.body.成立条件: Shared information or models produce similar operations, whose market effects encourage further operations in the same direction.
