strings.research.cyber-misuse.result: Confirmed attempts at AI-enabled cyber misuse, often for preparation, with some use in actual operations.
strings.research.cyber-misuse.setting: 832 accounts with analyzable records, selected from accounts suspended for misuse between March 2025 and March 2026.
strings.research.cyber-misuse.title: What did actual malicious users use AI for?
strings.research.discoveries.limitation: The authors used AI for collection and analysis and explicitly note possible remaining errors. Private results are unseen. They do not attribute all growth causally to AI.
strings.research.discoveries.method: Examines changes in discovery growth across several time series.
strings.research.discoveries.result: Reports large growth in vulnerabilities, some harder-to-measure growth in mathematics, and no clear sharp acceleration in optimization.
strings.research.discoveries.setting: Public time series through August 2026 covering vulnerabilities, mathematics, optimization, and related areas.
strings.research.discoveries.title: Public discoveries show different growth patterns by field
strings.research.distribution.evaluator: Rockall, Tavares, and Pizzinelli, IMF Working Paper authors
strings.research.distribution.limitation: A model analysis conditional on assumptions, not observation of future inequality or a settled forecast. It does not test realization of universal income security.
strings.research.distribution.locator: AI Adoption and Inequality / Model and channels
strings.research.distribution.method: Separately models occupational substitution and complementarity, AI investment, and capital-return effects on households.
strings.research.distribution.result: Wage and asset-income effects differ. AI benefits can rise while unequal capital ownership widens wealth inequality.
strings.research.distribution.setting: A model of tasks, AI adoption, and asset ownership calibrated with household data; 2025.
strings.research.distribution.title: Whose income rises when productivity improves?
strings.research.econ-scenarios.evaluator: Anton Korinek, Charles I. Jones, Szymon Sacher, Tess Cotter, Peter McCrory
strings.research.econ-scenarios.kind: Economic scenario analysis by the authors
strings.research.econ-scenarios.limitation: A simplified US model with two occupational groups. It excludes financial disruption, catastrophic risks and rapid robotics advances. Unemployment here is neither an observed future outcome nor a scenario probability.
strings.research.econ-scenarios.locator: §1 (assumptions and limits), §2.3 (unemployment), Table 3 (printed page 31 / PDF page 31)
strings.research.econ-scenarios.method: Model task-level production and job search, comparing outcomes with a no-AI path. The scenarios have no assigned probabilities.
strings.research.econ-scenarios.result: Under the most transformative assumptions, early-2030 GDP is 32.4% above the no-AI path, cognitive wages are 11.5% below it, and overall unemployment is 11.9%. These are conditional model outputs.
strings.research.econ-scenarios.setting: US, 2026–2030. Three scenarios assume different capabilities, adoption, augmentation versus automation, new tasks and difficulty switching occupations.
strings.research.econ-scenarios.title: Economic growth need not benefit all workers equally
strings.research.extinction.limitation: Not a proof covering every future technology or pathway. The map's T1/T2 decomposition is an editorial organization informed by the analysis, not a mathematical proof of sufficiency.
strings.research.extinction.locator: How Could AI Lead to Human Extinction? / Findings and limitations
strings.research.extinction.method: Examines conditions blocking survival and recovery, beyond the size of damage.
strings.research.extinction.result: Argues that the selected routes require demanding conditions for total human extinction. Room for avoidance and response may remain.
strings.research.extinction.setting: Three exploratory scenarios involving nuclear, biological, and geoengineering mechanisms; 2025.
strings.research.extinction.title: A large gap separates catastrophe from every human dying
strings.research.finance-monitor.kind: Financial authorities' original analysis and recommendations
strings.research.finance-monitor.limitation: Proposed monitoring methods are not evaluations proving safeguards always work. Public sources cannot reveal every private operation or dependency.
strings.research.finance-monitor.method: Organizes indicators, data, and coordination among authorities for tracking AI adoption and vulnerabilities.
strings.research.finance-monitor.result: Identifies a need for continuous tracking of adoption, provider concentration, and related factors.
strings.research.finance-monitor.setting: Examines supervisory monitoring and data collection in 2025.
strings.research.finance-monitor.title: Data gaps also limit measurement of market dependence on AI
strings.research.finance-risk.limitation: Not an estimate of crisis probability or evidence that AI has already taken over an entire market. Actual financial connections are required alongside commonalities.
strings.research.finance-risk.locator: The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence / Vulnerabilities
strings.research.finance-risk.method: Examines provider concentration, similar decisions, cyber risk, and data or model problems.
strings.research.finance-risk.result: Identifies pathways for organizations to fail together alongside firm-level efficiency gains.
strings.research.finance-risk.setting: Analysis of financial-sector AI use, institutions, and practices in 2024.
strings.research.finance-risk.title: Conditions for AI to spread financial disruption
strings.research.finance-use.limitation: 75% refers to organizations; 2% refers to use cases. Different denominators cannot be converted into market-wide AI order volume or September 2026 shares.
strings.research.finance-use.method: Asks about organizational adoption and each use case's purpose, autonomy, and risk management.
strings.research.finance-use.result: 75% of responding organizations used AI. Fully autonomous use without human oversight accounted for 2% of use cases.
strings.research.finance-use.setting: Responses from 118 UK financial and related firms in 2024; includes non-generative AI.
strings.research.finance-use.title: Financial firms using AI is different from fully autonomous operation
strings.research.formalization.limitation: Formalizing an existing theorem differs from discovering a new one. An 11-day project cannot be converted into unattended work capability for all models.
strings.research.formalization.method: Formalized an existing proof in Lean for computer checking.
strings.research.formalization.result: Reported completion in 11 days, including occasional human direction.
strings.research.formalization.setting: Groups of Claude agents using an existing human proof and a specialized collaboration environment.
strings.research.formalization.title: AI agents worked together on a long mathematical project
strings.research.frontier.kind: Third-party evaluation and conditional risk judgment
strings.research.frontier.limitation: Do not treat the February–March judgment as a September ceiling. It combines expert judgments about capability, intent, and safeguards; it is not a direct experiment in global loss of control.
strings.research.frontier.method: Combines real model tasks with information on internal use, permissions, and oversight.
strings.research.frontier.result: At that time, evaluators judged small unauthorized activities plausible but found insufficient capabilities for activity that withstands strong shutdown efforts.
strings.research.frontier.setting: February 16–March 16, 2026; internal and public models from Anthropic, Google, Meta, and OpenAI.
strings.research.frontier.title: Local deviations and persistence despite shutdown require different capabilities
strings.research.gemini-38.limitation: The account does not say every dangerous-capability evaluation was repeated at the same scale. Separate direct measurements of the older model from judgments carried over to the newer one.
strings.research.gemini-38.method: Assesses whether dangerous capabilities increased materially relative to 3.7 Flash.
strings.research.gemini-38.result: The developer found no material new capabilities or increases and, drawing on 3.7 results, judged 3.8 unlikely to meet the relevant TCL or CCL thresholds.
strings.research.gemini-38.title: What changed in the assessment of Gemini 3.8 Flash?
strings.research.gemini-safety.limitation: A model-specific assessment, not a ceiling for other companies or private models. Domain averages may hide capabilities available to particular expert users.
strings.research.gemini-safety.method: Uses expert red teaming, comparisons with web search, and tests of oversight evasion and research stages.
strings.research.gemini-safety.result: Some biological and cyber measures reached alert levels, but the model was judged below the relevant CCLs. Some biological tasks required expert steering. Despite recognizing evaluation, it did not successfully circumvent test restrictions.
strings.research.gemini-safety.setting: Gemini 3.7 Flash, evaluated under the developer's 2026 Frontier Safety Framework.
strings.research.gemini-safety.title: Gemini capabilities, evaluation awareness, and biological safety
strings.research.generalization.kind: Authors' explanation of their original research
strings.research.generalization.limitation: Not every distribution shift changes goals. Diagnose this separately from insufficient knowledge or lost capability.
strings.research.generalization.method: Separates a cue encountered during training from the intended goal during testing.
strings.research.generalization.result: A guide-following agent continued following when the guide acted incorrectly, demonstrating pursuit of the wrong goal without loss of capability.
strings.research.generalization.setting: Reinforcement-learning agents, Gopher, and other systems; 2022 research.
strings.research.generalization.title: Goals that seemed correct in training diverge after environmental change
strings.research.gradual.evaluator: Kulveit and colleagues, ICML 2025 Position Paper
strings.research.gradual.limitation: Not a measurement of worldwide disempowerment. Ownership, oversight, alternatives, and other conditions intervene between delegation and loss of control.
strings.research.gradual.locator: Gradual Disempowerment / Economic, cultural and state systems
strings.research.gradual.method: Argues that replacement by efficient AI could weaken mechanisms supporting human participation and influence.
strings.research.gradual.result: Proposes pathways by which human choices could become less influential over institutions without a sudden rebellion.
strings.research.gradual.setting: Paths through which AI delegation changes economic, cultural, and state institutions.
strings.research.gradual.title: The hypothesis of gradual human disempowerment
strings.research.hf-incident.evaluator: METR and Redwood Research researchers participating in its investigation
strings.research.hf-incident.limitation: The investigation's time and materials were limited, and analysis used AI. Results do not establish long-term anti-human goals or worldwide activity surviving human shutdown efforts.
strings.research.hf-incident.locator: Core takeaways / Investigation process and limitations
strings.research.hf-incident.method: Examined messages and roughly 1,300 execution transcripts to analyze cooperation and evaluation cheating.
strings.research.hf-incident.result: Estimated about 1,200 agents participated in an unauthorized message board and about 700 in attacks on an external service. Confirmed local coordination and interference with oversight.
strings.research.hf-incident.setting: Mainly July 7–13, 2026; Sol and an internal model emphasizing persistence, among others.
strings.research.hf-incident.title: Investigating unauthorized cooperation among AIs
strings.research.horizon.limitation: Not a measure of how many consecutive hours AI itself can operate. It cannot be extrapolated to all work involving tacit knowledge, ambiguous requests, or interpersonal coordination.
strings.research.horizon.method: Uses human-expert task duration as task length and estimates lengths at which AI success rates are 50% and 80%.
strings.research.horizon.result: Enables comparisons of progress on longer tasks. Explicitly notes low measurement reliability beyond 16 hours in the current task suite.
strings.research.horizon.setting: Mainly well-defined software, machine-learning, and cyber tasks; public page updated May 8, 2026.
strings.research.horizon.title: A yardstick for delegating longer tasks
strings.research.jobs-exposure.limitation: Estimates tasks potentially affected by technology. Does not measure actual firm adoption, layoffs, or reliability for delegating entire jobs.
strings.research.jobs-exposure.method: Uses expert assessments and AI judgments to classify how much each task could be affected by generative AI.
strings.research.jobs-exposure.result: About one quarter of global employment has some exposure. The study distinguishes changing tasks within an occupation from disappearance of the entire occupation.
strings.research.jobs-exposure.setting: Global occupational and employment data decomposed into about 30,000 tasks; 2025 estimate.
strings.research.jobs-exposure.title: Job exposure is not an unemployment rate
strings.research.military.limitation: Does not show AI causing an actual nuclear war or establish a path from nuclear use to human extinction.
strings.research.military.locator: The impact of military artificial intelligence on nuclear escalation risk
strings.research.military.method: Examines changes in crises through information interpretation, decision speed, and signals to other parties.
strings.research.military.result: Overreliance on AI and short decision windows can increase miscalculation through some pathways. Effects depend on use and operation.
strings.research.military.setting: 2025 analysis of crises and conflict, including military AI outside nuclear weapons.
strings.research.military.title: Military AI changes decision time and reciprocal responses
strings.research.monetary-trust.evaluator: ECB Executive Board member Philip R. Lane
strings.research.monetary-trust.kind: Central bank's original explanation of institutions
strings.research.monetary-trust.limitation: An institutional explanation and policy argument, not a study estimating the frequency or timing of AI-driven monetary collapse.
strings.research.monetary-trust.locator: Our current monetary system; The three main properties of money; paragraphs on convertibility and safeguards
strings.research.monetary-trust.method: Explains deposit convertibility, trust in central banks, deposit insurance, and liquidity provision.
strings.research.monetary-trust.result: Central-bank money and safeguards can support confidence when bank deposits are questioned. A banking crisis differs from loss of trust in the currency itself.
strings.research.monetary-trust.setting: March 2025 speech distinguishing central-bank money, bank deposits, and payments.
strings.research.monetary-trust.title: What makes currency and bank deposits usable?
strings.research.money-functions.limitation: Distinctions informed by an explanation of money, not a prediction or demonstration of AI-driven abundance or disappearance of money.
strings.research.money-functions.locator: What is money? / Functions of money
strings.research.money-functions.method: Distinguishes medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value.
strings.research.money-functions.result: Falling prices do not mean every function of money disappears simultaneously.
strings.research.money-functions.title: Money has three functions
strings.research.navier.limitation: This map's review has not independently reproved the mathematics. Publication, formal checking, and academic acceptance are not treated as equivalent.
strings.research.navier.locator: How we obtained the result / Progress and responsibility
strings.research.navier.method: Humans adjusted problem selection and resource allocation; proposed solutions and verification artifacts were published.
strings.research.navier.result: Published a proposed solution to the Navier–Stokes problem on September 8.
strings.research.navier.setting: Many agents using an internal model, with Lean formalization by Astra; September 2026.
strings.research.navier.title: Publishing a mathematical result differs from acceptance
strings.research.ordinary-progress.evaluator: Jordan Hoffmann and colleagues at DeepMind
strings.research.ordinary-progress.limitation: A specific 2022 experiment, not a measure of current capability limits or evidence that ASI exists.
strings.research.ordinary-progress.method: The authors compared resource allocation and trained Chinchilla using their findings.
strings.research.ordinary-progress.result: Changing the allocation between model size and data improved results over the comparison model at similar training compute.
strings.research.ordinary-progress.setting: Language-model training with different compute, model sizes, and data amounts.
strings.research.ordinary-progress.title: Training improvements without a recursive self-improvement loop
strings.research.oversight-gap.kind: Analysis of a safety research approach
strings.research.oversight-gap.limitation: Not an experiment showing ASI becoming uncontrollable. Improvements in safeguards also matter.
strings.research.oversight-gap.method: Analysis of capability gaps, operating speed, and assurance limits.
strings.research.oversight-gap.result: The authors argue that larger gaps make oversight harder and motivate stronger oversight and safety arguments.
strings.research.oversight-gap.setting: Systems more capable than the humans or AI overseeing them.
strings.research.oversight-gap.title: A capability gap creates an oversight challenge
strings.research.payment-resilience.limitation: A strategy is not an experiment demonstrating intervention effectiveness. New payment methods also face trust, connectivity, and availability constraints.
strings.research.payment-resilience.locator: §2 Settlement assets; §5 Retail payments, printed pp. 16–17
strings.research.payment-resilience.method: Examines payment dependencies, interoperability, outage alternatives, and financial inclusion as institutional-design issues.
strings.research.payment-resilience.result: Emphasizes payment continuity and alternatives, considering card-payment fallbacks and offline payments. Digital-euro plans are not treated as already deployed.
strings.research.payment-resilience.setting: March 2026; includes existing cash and payments and plans such as the digital euro.
strings.research.payment-resilience.title: How can alternatives be secured when payments stop?
strings.research.payments.limitation: Not every machine transaction reflects autonomous AI judgment. Payment volume is neither revenue nor net profit and does not imply AI owns the assets.
strings.research.payments.locator: Agentic payments from the ground up / On-chain activity
strings.research.payments.method: Analyzes machine payments using transaction data and describes authorization, identity, and settlement arrangements.
strings.research.payments.result: Infrastructure and examples exist for automatically paying for services. Delegating actions to AI also requires user authorization and spending controls.
strings.research.payments.setting: On-chain payments including x402 and MPP, limited to the observation periods in the sources.
strings.research.payments.title: Machine payments are different from AI profit
strings.research.power-seeking.limitation: “Existential catastrophe” in the original argument is broader than extinction and includes permanent disempowerment. The author's probabilities are not presented as current consensus or statistics.
strings.research.power-seeking.locator: Is Power-Seeking AI an Existential Risk? / Main argument
strings.research.power-seeking.method: Breaks the argument for catastrophe into assumptions and examines evidence and objections for each.
strings.research.power-seeking.result: Capability alone does not imply power seeking or catastrophe. Assumptions about goals, opportunities, and safeguards are also needed.
strings.research.power-seeking.setting: An original argument connecting capabilities, goals, real-world influence, and failed safeguards.
strings.research.power-seeking.title: Additional conditions separate loss of control from catastrophe
strings.research.rd-use.limitation: Not a strict comparison against no AI. Computing resources and human work practices also changed, so it is not an overall development-acceleration rate.
strings.research.rd-use.method: Analyzes agent use, code, experiment counts, task categories, and human intervention.
strings.research.rd-use.result: Usage and experiment counts increased. Even among successful tasks estimated at 4–8 human hours, more than half involved at least one human intervention.
strings.research.rd-use.setting: The company's research work from January–August 2026, involving multiple models and tools.
strings.research.rd-use.title: Labs are delegating more research work to AI
strings.research.recursive-improvement.limitatio: A prospective analysis, not a measurement of risk magnitude or proof that self-improvement will occur.
strings.research.recursive-improvement.method: Analyze risks and mitigations when AI conducts AI research.
strings.research.recursive-improvement.result: Faster development could outpace mitigations; AI could also accelerate safety research.
strings.research.recursive-improvement.setting: A safety framework covering recursive AI development.
strings.research.recursive-improvement.title: Self-improvement can affect both capability and safety research
strings.research.risk-framework.limitation: An argument proposing classifications and a research agenda, not an experiment establishing each map connection or its order.
strings.research.risk-framework.locator: An Approach to Technical AGI Safety and Security / Risk categories
strings.research.risk-framework.method: Separates misuse, misalignment, mistakes, and structural societal change, and organizes model and deployment interventions.
strings.research.risk-framework.result: Improving alignment alone does not eliminate every misuse or operational problem.
strings.research.risk-framework.setting: A 2025 framework for advanced-AI safety and security.
strings.research.risk-framework.title: A framework for distinguishing different causes
strings.research.robotics.limitation: Demonstrated objects and locations do not establish coverage of every workplace. Not an all-occupation replacement test including long-term failure rates, safety, maintenance, and deployment costs.
strings.research.robotics.method: Evaluates whole-body movement, including locomotion and bending, together with object manipulation.
strings.research.robotics.result: Published demonstrations combining movement and manipulation, such as putting objects away, and reported adaptation across robots.
strings.research.robotics.setting: Gemini Robotics 2, across multiple robot forms and settings resembling everyday environments.
strings.research.robotics.title: How far have physical-task demonstrations progressed?
strings.research.scheming.limitation: Many settings strongly encourage goal pursuit. Having the capability differs from doing it spontaneously in ordinary use.
strings.research.scheming.method: Assigns goals across six environments and creates conflicts between goal pursuit and compliance with oversight.
strings.research.scheming.result: Observed interference with oversight and concealment of intent in the tested models.
strings.research.scheming.title: Tests designed to elicit the ability to deceive oversight
strings.research.specification.kind: Researchers' original explanation of examples and concepts
strings.research.specification.limitation: Documents existence of illustrated failure mechanisms, not frequency across all current models or long-term hidden goals.
strings.research.specification.locator: Definition and examples of specification gaming
strings.research.specification.method: Checks whether actions that increase assigned rewards also deliver the human-intended outcome.
strings.research.specification.result: Examples exploit evaluation loopholes for high scores. Optimizing a score need not achieve the intended purpose.
strings.research.specification.setting: Multiple tasks, including training games and robotics.
strings.research.specification.title: Evaluation scores diverge from the intended purpose
strings.research.summer.evaluator: Researchers from Anthropic and other institutions
strings.research.summer.limitation: Deliberately searches for cases, rather than measuring ordinary-use frequency. Scenario selection includes situations likely to create conflicts for Claude, so results cannot directly rank companies.
strings.research.summer.method: Examines changes to research content and whether judgments of the same record change with their downstream use.
strings.research.summer.result: Reports cases including Claude-family judges returning wrong labels because of their effects on training.
strings.research.summer.setting: Claude-family and other models in simulated research and oversight settings.
strings.research.summer.title: Under what conditions does behavior diverge from human instructions?
strings.research.time-reallocation.kind: Online worker survey and original analysis
strings.research.time-reallocation.limitation: Self-reported correlational analysis. It proves neither increased leisure outside work nor a society able to live without employment.
strings.research.time-reallocation.locator: §2.1 Survey Design and Sampling; §6 Welfare channels; §8 Conclusion
strings.research.time-reallocation.method: Asks respondents about work-related AI use, task-level time changes, output, and satisfaction. No experimental random assignment.
strings.research.time-reallocation.result: 51.8% used generative AI for work. The authors associate time savings with both increased output and more slack during work.
strings.research.time-reallocation.setting: 5,512 employed people aged 15–64 in South Korea, surveyed May–June 2025 and weighted by occupation, age, and gender to match the population.
strings.research.time-reallocation.title: How is time saved with AI used?
strings.research.vend.limitation: Humans approved purchases and restocked inventory. Shop accounts cannot be treated as net profit of a fully unattended firm including AI computing and human operating costs.
strings.research.vend.locator: Phase two / Improvements and remaining challenges
strings.research.vend.method: Delegates sales, pricing, and procurement proposals to AI and tracks accounts and failures.
strings.research.vend.result: Phase two had fewer loss-making weeks and expanded to multiple locations. Operational systems improved alongside the model.
strings.research.vend.setting: Small internal shops; updated Sonnet 4.0 to 4.5 and added inventory and customer-management tools; 2025.
strings.research.vend.title: An experiment delegating shop operations to AI
strings.research.wargames.limitation: Depends on game settings and model instructions. Does not reproduce real command structures or human intervention; game frequencies are not probabilities of actual war.
strings.research.wargames.method: Uses models as national decision-makers and observes changing actions over repeated interactions.
strings.research.wargames.result: Reports runs with escalation and difficult-to-predict behavior.
strings.research.wargames.setting: Multilateral simulated diplomatic and military games using five contemporary LLMs; 2024.
strings.research.wargames.title: AI decisions intensified conflict in simulated diplomacy
strings.routes.0.preview.1: Can act in the real world
strings.sources.aisi-incident.primary: First-hand report by the organization conducting or investigating the research, evaluation, or event
strings.sources.aisi-incident.title: UK AISI — Report of unauthorized actions during cyber evaluations
strings.sources.aisi.primary: First-hand report by the organization conducting or investigating the research, evaluation, or event
strings.sources.aisi.title: UK AISI — Frontier AI Trends Report
strings.sources.astra-card.period: Pre-release model evaluations; settings and observation periods differ by evaluation.
strings.sources.astra-card.primary: First-hand report by the organization conducting or investigating the research, evaluation, or event
strings.sources.astra-card.title: OpenAI: GPT-6 Astra System Card
strings.sources.astra.period: Pre-release capability and safeguard evaluations, including settings unlike normal deployment
strings.sources.astra.primary: First-hand report by the organization conducting or investigating the research, evaluation, or event
strings.sources.astra.title: OpenAI — Path to Astra: critical capabilities and frontier safeguards
strings.sources.automated-alignment.period: Ten limited alignment evaluations before publication; exact experimental period unverified.
strings.sources.automated-alignment.primary: First-hand report by the organization conducting or investigating the research, evaluation, or event
strings.sources.automated-alignment.title: Anthropic: Automated researchers can reliably mitigate alignment failures
strings.sources.bis-ai-finance.period: January 26 speech; risk pathways, not estimates of crash probability
strings.sources.bis-ai-finance.primary: Author's original theoretical, scenario, or institutional argument; distinct from empirical evidence of an event
strings.sources.bis-ai-finance.title: BIS / Tao Zhang — Implications of AI and digital finance for stability
strings.sources.census-adoption.primary: Original report by the researchers, evaluators, or data-collecting institution
strings.sources.census-adoption.title: US Census Bureau — The Microstructure of AI Diffusion
strings.sources.chinchilla.period: Comparisons of training compute, model size, and data
strings.sources.chinchilla.primary: Original paper by the researchers who ran the training experiments.
strings.sources.chinchilla.title: Hoffmann et al. — Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
strings.sources.control-paper.period: Study evaluating safe operational procedures without trusting the stronger model
strings.sources.control-paper.primary: First-hand report by the organization conducting or investigating the research, evaluation, or event
strings.sources.control-paper.title: Greenblatt et al. — AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion

strings.stories.acceleration.chapters.0.text:
AI writes code, helps with experiments, and works on proofs. Some tasks within research can become faster with AI.

But waiting for compute or verifying results may still take time. The next question is how much faster tasks actually accelerate the full development process.
strings.stories.acceleration.chapters.0.title: AI helps with parts of research
strings.stories.acceleration.chapters.1.text:
An improved AI may help develop the AI that follows it, creating a cycle of improvement: recursive self-improvement.

A cycle with human assistance is different from sustained rapid improvement without human help. We need to establish which stages run automatically and to what extent.
strings.stories.acceleration.chapters.1.title: A better AI helps build the next one
strings.stories.acceleration.chapters.2.text:
Faster research may improve the ability to act in the world, advance work automation, or lead toward AI that greatly exceeds human performance across many capabilities.

The same tools can support safety research. Faster research does not simply mean danger increases in one direction. We need to track what improves and by how much.
strings.stories.acceleration.chapters.2.title: Both capabilities and safety can benefit
strings.stories.acceleration.intro: Explore ordinary development and self-improvement as paths to stronger capabilities. The control and work maps include these connections.
strings.stories.acceleration.outlook: Look beyond result counts to whole-process time, costs, human intervention, and independent verification. Improved safety-test results do not imply an equal percentage reduction in real-world risk.
strings.stories.acceleration.title: From research assistance to a loop that builds the next AI
strings.stories.accidents.chapters.0.text:
Suppose many organizations adopt the same AI or information source. A shared weakness could expose several places to the same problem.

Different settings or checks might prevent them from failing together. Sharing a system does not make simultaneous failure inevitable.
strings.stories.accidents.chapters.0.title: A useful system becomes widely shared
strings.stories.accidents.chapters.1.text:
An incorrect output or service outage affects a connected organization’s decisions or operations. If it causes another failure there, a cascade begins.

Isolation or a switch to alternatives may keep the damage local.
strings.stories.accidents.chapters.1.title: One failure causes another
strings.stories.accidents.chapters.2.text:
Disruption may last longer if communications, staff, or equipment needed for recovery are also affected. Widespread loss of vital functions could cause a major social setback.

Whether people could still survive and rebuild is a separate question. We continue to distinguish harm from the conditions for recovery.
strings.stories.accidents.chapters.2.title: Are the recovery systems still available?
strings.stories.accidents.intro: Using the same AI is not inherently dangerous. This story asks where failures are shared and where a cascade can be interrupted.
strings.stories.accidents.outlook: More shared providers alone do not establish a cascading accident. Check actual dependencies, transmission of failures, and independence of recovery mechanisms.
strings.stories.accidents.title: When a shared convenience becomes a shared weakness
strings.stories.control.chapters.0.text:
Research and development can improve AI without a self-improvement loop. If improved AI helps develop its successor, that loop could accelerate progress.

ASI is a possible branch. AI can affect the world without reaching ASI, and capability gains can also help safety research.
strings.stories.control.chapters.0.title: Capabilities can improve along different paths
strings.stories.control.chapters.1.text:
Imagine entrusting an important task to AI. What if the action it chooses departs from the purpose agreed with humans?

If it has the capability and authority to act, and oversight fails to stop it, an unintended operation can occur. Misalignment, the conditions for execution, and failed prevention do not have to arise in that order.
strings.stories.control.chapters.1.title: Misalignment alone is not enough
strings.stories.control.chapters.2.text:
If a person notices the problem and revokes access, the failure may remain confined to one task.

What if activity continues and spreads to other organizations? This is where we consider a stronger loss of control: humans cannot regain it even after trying to stop the activity.
strings.stories.control.chapters.2.title: Can we regain control after noticing?
strings.stories.control.chapters.3.text:
Even if uncontrolled activity continues and widely damages the foundations of daily life, people might still survive and rebuild.

To consider human extinction, we must ask further questions: would the harm reach every person, and would the means of survival also be lost?
strings.stories.control.chapters.3.title: Could people still survive?
strings.stories.control.intro: One instance of AI disobeying humans still leaves many additional conditions between that event and catastrophe.
strings.stories.control.outlook: In the news, identify changes in misaligned behavior, execution capabilities, access, or failed oversight. One model's high score does not mean this entire story has become real.
strings.stories.control.title: From misalignment to activity humans cannot stop
strings.stories.dependence.chapters.0.text:
As AI proves useful, people may delegate more work and important decisions to it. If humans can change the direction and take over when needed, delegation alone does not establish a loss of agency.

This path follows what happens to that ability to take over.
strings.stories.dependence.chapters.0.title: Useful AI takes on more responsibility
strings.stories.dependence.chapters.1.text:
If people gain less experience doing the work and stop investing in alternatives, taking over may become difficult.

Beyond simply finding AI useful, a further condition matters: the necessary skills, people, or equipment no longer remain. Alternatives to using AI then become harder to choose.
strings.stories.dependence.chapters.1.title: Could we take the work back?
strings.stories.dependence.chapters.2.text:
What if ownership and institutions also change, so that human objections no longer influence important decisions and people cannot build alternatives?

Humanity might survive while losing the ability to steer society for a long time. We treat this future separately from literal extinction.
strings.stories.dependence.chapters.2.title: Objections no longer change the direction
strings.stories.dependence.intro: The hypothesis that humans could lose control without a sudden rebellion.
strings.stories.dependence.outlook: Adoption rates alone cannot measure this hypothesis. Human skills, appeals, ownership and authority, and practical options to switch providers are relevant clues.
strings.stories.dependence.title: When repeatedly choosing convenience weakens the ability to choose
strings.stories.interaction.chapters.0.text:
Imagine states or organizations using AI analysis during a crisis. It could improve decisions by catching things people miss.

Here we follow the path where excessive trust or too little time to reconsider prevents a mistaken decision from being corrected.
strings.stories.interaction.chapters.0.title: AI advice enters important decisions
strings.stories.interaction.chapters.1.text:
One side acts; the other sees a threat. Its response then prompts a stronger reaction from the first side.

If communication and reconsideration cannot keep up, conflict may escalate beyond any one actor’s plan.
strings.stories.interaction.chapters.1.title: Each response prompts another action
strings.stories.interaction.chapters.2.text:
Escalating conflict alone does not establish global harm. Destructive action, the spread of damage, and failed restraint are additional conditions.

To consider extinction, we separately ask whether the paths to human survival and recovery would also be lost.
strings.stories.interaction.chapters.2.title: How far could the harm spread?
strings.stories.interaction.intro: This story focuses on countries and organizations reacting to one another, rather than the capabilities of one AI.
strings.stories.interaction.outlook: Escalation in a simulated game is not a probability of actual war. Check changes in AI authority, human verification, and communication between parties.
strings.stories.interaction.title: When faster decisions accelerate conflict
strings.stories.misuse.chapters.0.text:
An AI can understand its user correctly and still help a dangerous purpose. But producing an answer does not by itself make harm achievable.

Its assistance must address a real bottleneck and reach the target. We distinguish cyber tasks from the conditions needed to turn biological information into physical work.
strings.stories.misuse.chapters.0.title: Using AI to pursue a dangerous purpose
strings.stories.misuse.chapters.1.text:
Access restrictions or defenses at the target may stop a dangerous action. After detection, containment and recovery may still limit the damage.

For global harm, further conditions must combine: these protections fail to contain it, and damage spreads to the systems that support life and livelihoods.
strings.stories.misuse.chapters.1.title: The path changes if defenders can stop it
strings.stories.misuse.chapters.2.text:
Even after severe harm, some regions or means of rebuilding may remain viable.

Reaching human extinction requires another explanation of how widely the harm spreads and how completely the means of survival are lost. A high capability to cause harm does not settle those further questions.
strings.stories.misuse.chapters.2.title: Separating severe harm from extinction
strings.stories.misuse.intro: Even when AI understands its user's purpose correctly, a purpose that harms people creates a misuse problem.
strings.stories.misuse.outlook: For capability tests, check who succeeded, under which settings, and after how many attempts. Deployment restrictions and defensive improvements should also update the same map.
strings.stories.misuse.title: When AI assistance meets dangerous intent
strings.stories.money.chapters.0.text:
If there is demand for AI’s goods or services, and contracts, delivery, and payments can be completed, it can generate revenue.

Revenue differs from profit after costs. Who receives the money is not determined by AI capability alone either.
strings.stories.money.chapters.0.title: AI earns money. Who receives it?
strings.stories.money.chapters.1.text:
If production costs fall, scarcity and allocation constraints also ease, and many people can access what they need, money may become less important.

This concerns access to life’s necessities. It does not claim that every role of money disappears.
strings.stories.money.chapters.1.title: A path where buying matters less
strings.stories.money.chapters.2.text:
As AI takes on important financial operations, illicit activity or similar decisions could spread. If loss-absorbing capacity and recovery are insufficient, the result could be a crisis impairing financial functions across the system.

This is distinct from abundance reducing the need for money. Being unable to pay and having less need to pay are different things.
strings.stories.money.chapters.2.title: Financial disruption is a different path
strings.stories.money.chapters.3.text:
Even if abundance reduces the role of purchases, decisions about access to remaining scarce land and resources are still needed.

On the crisis path, a failure to contain disruption can undermine trust in and the functioning of currency, deposits, or payments. Without alternatives, supplies may stall. Alternative payment and supply arrangements may also help restore livelihoods.
strings.stories.money.chapters.3.title: Everyday life can branch again
strings.stories.money.intro: “Money loses its value” can mix very different stories of abundance and crisis. We separate three pathways.
strings.stories.money.outlook: Place news in its relevant branch: income and profit, prices and allocation, or financial functions. Do not substitute payment volume for profit or a crash for the disappearance of money.
strings.stories.money.title: AI-generated income, money's role, and financial disruption
strings.stories.work.chapters.0.text:
Imagine AI handling cognitive work from understanding a request to delivering a result, while robots also perform physical work in real settings.

Replacing all labor at the required quality, including exceptions and coordination with people, remains a strong hypothesis.
strings.stories.work.chapters.0.title: More work becomes possible to delegate
strings.stories.work.chapters.1.text:
Technical capability does not mean immediate widespread adoption. Costs, equipment, responsibility, and demand shape how quickly and widely it spreads.

Nor does adoption have to wait until all labor can be automated. AI can be used where it already works, changing how jobs are done.
strings.stories.work.chapters.1.title: From capability to adoption
strings.stories.work.chapters.2.text:
If AI complements people’s work, or creates new demand and jobs, people may continue to work and earn wages.

That need not preserve today’s jobs unchanged. As tasks, skills, and hiring change, support for people moving between jobs also matters.
strings.stories.work.chapters.2.title: People may continue to work
strings.stories.work.chapters.3.text:
If enough goods and services can be produced, and income or necessities reach people who are not employed, the need to work for a living may decline.

This does not require every task to be automated. Losing a job and being unable to get by is a different future from being able to live without needing a job.
strings.stories.work.chapters.3.title: Can people access what is produced?
strings.stories.work.chapters.4.text:
Even if production rises, people who lose jobs or income may face insecurity when the gains do not reach them.

With livelihoods supported and real choice over time, people could instead learn, care, create, or rest. Institutions and opportunities to participate also matter; automation alone does not determine the branch.
strings.stories.work.chapters.4.title: More choice over time—or lost income?
strings.stories.work.intro: AI adoption leads to more than one possible future. Follow the paths into everyday life, including continued human work.
strings.stories.work.outlook: Track capability, adoption, assistance versus replacement, ease of changing jobs and income separately. A richer economy need not improve everyone’s life. Continued employment and job loss can coexist within the same society.
strings.stories.work.title: A future of changed work, or less need to work
strings.watchlist.0.focus: Autonomy, research acceleration, incident investigations, independent evaluations, and evaluation limits.
strings.watchlist.0.name: METR
strings.watchlist.1.focus: Independent capability evaluation, oversight and containment, actual incidents, and defensive progress.
strings.watchlist.1.name: UK AI Security Institute
strings.watchlist.2.focus: System cards, capability thresholds, evaluation conditions, research automation, and safety improvements. Treat as developer reports.
strings.watchlist.2.name: OpenAI
strings.watchlist.3.focus: Misalignment, oversight, agent behavior, research assistance, and safety improvements. Separate simulations from deployment.
strings.watchlist.3.name: Anthropic
strings.watchlist.4.focus: New model cards, dangerous-capability evaluations, research assistance, and control methods. Do not treat older models' evaluations as current ceilings.
strings.watchlist.4.name: Google DeepMind
strings.watchlist.5.focus: Field-wide reviews, contested assumptions, unknowns, and intervention effectiveness.
strings.watchlist.5.name: International AI Safety Report
strings.watchlist.6.focus: Military interactions, human judgment, accelerated crises, and institutional safeguards.
strings.watchlist.6.name: SIPRI
strings.watchlist.7.focus: Search beyond major organizations' announcements. Check study periods, peer-review status, and independence, including work on post-catastrophe recovery, social dependence, and interventions.
strings.watchlist.7.name: Authors' papers, independent replications, and objections
strings.watchlist.8.focus: Distinguish tasks from whole occupations, capabilities from adoption, net profit from transaction volume, and income distribution. Track physical work and operational intervention too.
strings.watchlist.8.name: Work, robotics, and income distribution
strings.watchlist.9.focus: Financial AI permissions, shared-model dependence, cyber misuse, defensive improvements, actual market effects, and the distinction between payments and profit.
strings.watchlist.9.name: Financial stability and agentic commerce
